source_text: In Jewish society, mohels are generally revered as skilled ritual specialists essential to covenantal identity, with selections prioritizing piety, competence, and experience; non-Jewish families increasingly hire them for precision and cultural appeal, citing lower infection risks compared to hospital settings.
